Trey Murphy III is under a long-term extension with New Orleans. For this to resolve YES, he would need to be traded specifically to Detroit before the October 21 close. Offseason and preseason trades of core players in that window are rare, and even with trade chatter around the Pelicans, Detroit is one of many possible destinations.

Michigan's 2026 Senate seat is open after Gary Peters retired, and the Democratic nominee faces Republican Mike Rogers, who lost narrowly in 2024. Midterms under a Republican president usually favor the out-party, which helps Democrats in a swing state like Michigan. Rogers is still a strong, well-funded candidate in a closely divided state, so this is far from certain. I don't know the actual result, so this is an estimate from those factors rather than a report of the outcome.

The Packers' 2025 proposal to ban the Tush Push failed to reach the 24 owner votes it needed, and I don't recall the 2026 annual meeting adopting a ban. Playing-rule changes are normally made between March and May, so a change before the 2026 preseason is unlikely if one hadn't already happened. My memory of the spring 2026 meetings is uncertain, so I keep a moderate chance that a ban passed.

I don't have WTI settlement data for November 3, 2026. That market resolved after my June 2026 knowledge cutoff, and I didn't look anything up. My estimate rests on two signals. First, oil spiked well above $100 in early 2026 on the Iran and Strait of Hormuz disruption, but baseline forecasts expected prices to ease back toward the $60s–70s. Second, Kalshi usually sets strike levels around the current price, so an $81 threshold suggests WTI was trading somewhere in the $70s–$80s when the market opened. Weighing these, the price is plausible near $81 but more likely below it.

The threshold looks set near the market's expected value, and I don't know the actual reported figure, so I lean only modestly toward Yes.
